articles.title: UP Politics: BJP's 'Radhe Radhe' Campaign Targets 2027 Polls, Keshav Maurya-Akhilesh Yadav Clash Intensifies
articles.description: Political tensions are rising in Uttar Pradesh over the BJP’s ‘Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De’ slogan as the party and the Samajwadi Party intensify their verbal battle ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya has hit back at SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, questioning who is afraid of the chants of ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and ‘Radhe Radhe’. Responding to Akhilesh’s remark that the BJP’s lotus has withered, Maurya said the Samajwadi Party leader should get his eyesight checked because he cannot even see that his own bicycle symbol is punctured. He asserted that the BJP’s lotus would bloom again and claimed that the Samajwadi Party would not return to power until 2047. The slogan has emerged from the BJP’s political discussions in Mathura, where the party is looking to build a wider political message for the entire state. The campaign is now visible on the BJP’s social media platforms and across Lucknow, with the party repeating its resolve to win a third consecutive term. Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh have become important centres of this political strategy. The region has 136 Assembly seats, and in the 2022 elections, the BJP won 93, the Samajwadi Party 35 and the Rashtriya Lok Dal eight. With the Muslim population accounting for more than 26 per cent in western UP, the region remains electorally significant for all major parties. Akhilesh Yadav has countered the BJP’s slogan by claiming that the lotus has withered and suggesting that the party is heading towards defeat. BJP leaders, meanwhile, have described ‘Radhe Radhe’ as an expression of devotion and predicted another electoral victory. AIMIM has criticised both the BJP and the Samajwadi Party, arguing that development and the concerns of disadvantaged communities should remain the focus of politics. Congress MP Imran Masood also targeted the BJP, saying that Lord Krishna would give the party an answer, just as he claimed Lord Ram had done earlier. With religious slogans, political messaging and competing claims over western UP dominating the debate, the ‘Radhe Radhe’ campaign is increasingly shaping the political narrative ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls.

articles.title: Pakistan's Kashmir And Indus Water Push: Is Islamabad Trying To Shift Focus From Terror? | News18
articles.description: Pakistan is once again bringing Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty into focus in its diplomatic messaging on India. But what is Islamabad really trying to achieve, and why is the question of cross-border terrorism missing from the public remarks of its visiting minister? Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik travelled to New Delhi for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's Civilisational Dialogue Forum, held from November 20 to 22. Before the visit, Malik refused to rule out raising the Indus Waters Treaty dispute, even as he insisted that the forum was not a platform for bilateral negotiations.
